original_question: Let K be a number field, let f : PN → PN be an endomorphism of degree at least 2 defined over K, and let P ∈ PN (K) be a point that is not periodic for f . Then (f, P ) is eventually stable over K.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 19.9 in Section 19 ("Irreducibility and Stability of Iterates"), i.e. the higher-dimensional eventual-stability conjecture for a point P ∈ P^N(K). ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient field (a number field K), the correct map (an endomorphism f: P^N → P^N of degree at least 2 defined over K), the correct point hypothesis (P ∈ P^N(K) not periodic for f), and the correct conclusion ((f, P) is eventually stable over K). In fact, this is essentially Conjecture 19.9 verbatim once the paper's Definition 19.8 of eventual stability is supplied. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
missing_details: The draft does not define "eventually stable" in the paper's higher-dimensional sense. For a proper r-dimensional subvariety X ⊂ P^N defined over K, the paper writes f*X = Σ_{Y/K⊂P^N, dim(Y)=r, Y irreducible over K} m(f, X; Y)Y, and then defines (f, X) to be eventually stable over K if there is a constant C(f, X) such that sup_{n≥1} Σ_Y m(f^n, X; Y) ≤ C(f, X). For your point case, one must specialize this with X = P as a 0-dimensional subvariety. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

It leaves implicit that the summation is over K-irreducible subvarieties Y of the same dimension as X, and that m(f^n, X; Y) is the multiplicity of Y in the pullback (f^n)*X. Those ingredients are part of the paper's chosen formulation and are needed for a stand-alone statement. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

It does not indicate that this is the point-case analogue of the one-variable notion introduced earlier in the same section, where eventual stability is first defined for f(x) ∈ K(x) and α ∈ K and then generalized to higher-dimensional endomorphisms of P^N. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The draft does not make explicit that "not periodic" is the only dynamical restriction in Conjecture 19.9; the conjecture is not restricted to wandering points, so nonperiodic preperiodic points are included as well. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

To be fully paper-faithful and stand-alone, the statement should say that P is being regarded as a 0-dimensional subvariety of P^N when invoking Definition 19.8. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
refined_question:
Let K be a number field, let f: P^N → P^N be an endomorphism of degree at least 2 defined over K, and let P ∈ P^N(K) be a point that is not periodic for f. Viewing P as a 0-dimensional subvariety of P^N, write for each n ≥ 1
(f^n)*P = Σ_{Y/K⊂P^N, dim(Y)=0, Y irreducible over K} m(f^n, P; Y)Y.
Is there a constant C(f, P) such that
sup_{n≥1} Σ_{Y/K⊂P^N, dim(Y)=0, Y irreducible over K} m(f^n, P; Y) ≤ C(f, P)?
Equivalently, is the pair (f, P) eventually stable over K in the sense of Definition 19.8? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Conjecture 19.9, not a broader neighboring problem: the wording, ambient space P^N, degree restriction, nonperiodicity hypothesis, and conclusion all match that conjecture. The only substantive omission is that Conjecture 19.9 depends on Definition 19.8 for the meaning of "eventually stable" in higher dimension, and the immediately following Question 19.10 shows that the paper treats the point case as distinct from the broader subvariety case. So the sharpest refinement is to keep the point case exactly as stated in Conjecture 19.9 while spelling out Definition 19.8 specialized to X = P. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
